memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'Do not offer to the LORD the blind, the injured or the maimed, or
anything with warts or festering or running sores. Do not place any of
these on the altar as a food offering presented to the LORD. You may,
however, present as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep that is
deformed or stunted, but it will not be accepted in fulfillment of a
vow'" - Lev 22:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The list is deliberately specific. God closed every loophole. A person
could not look at his flock, pick out the weakest animal, and call it
generosity.

But notice verse 23 carefully. There was a small allowance. A deformed
or stunted animal could be given as a freewill offering - a gift
brought spontaneously - though not to fulfil a vow. Why the difference?
Because a vow was a promise. When you have made a commitment to God,
you do not get to quietly downgrade it later.

Dear reader, that principle is worth holding on to. We often make
promises to God in moments of desperation or deep gratitude, and then
renegotiate them once life settles down. Ecclesiastes warns us not to
be quick to make vows, and to fulfil the ones we make (Eccl 5:4-5).
Jesus taught that our simple yes should mean yes (Matt 5:37).

God is not a business partner to be bargained with. He is a Father to
be trusted and a King to be honoured.

If you promised Him something, keep it. If you cannot, tell Him
honestly rather than quietly slipping away.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I made a promise to God that I have quietly let slide?
2. Where am I tempted to look for shortcuts in my walk with God?
3. Do my words to God carry the weight they should?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for promises I made and did not keep. Give me
integrity in my words to You and to others, and help me follow through.
Amen.
